title: Odile and the Ghost
premise: Lior Marchetti, a private security contractor with a fabricated past, is guarding a delegation en route to a Geneva summit when the aircraft's records vanish mid-flight and the plane lands carrying one passenger fewer than it took off with. Hunting the missing man — a whistleblower holding proof that the summit's security architecture was built on Lior's own erased crimes — he is forced to ally with Odile Vasseur, an assassin whose target list and his own history share a single author. As three governments race to bury the flight, Lior must choose between protecting his polished lie and detonating it publicly. In the end, he delivers the truth at the summit itself, sacrificing his career and letting Odile walk away, while the ghost of the vanished passenger becomes the scandal no government can erase.
about_author: Kestrel Marchetti is a former aviation risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients she still cannot name. She writes thrillers from a coastal town in Portugal, where she keeps a go-bag out of habit.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. We meet him running close protection for a disreputable delegation, lying smoothly about his name and history during a vetting interview. The chapter establishes his polished lie, his packed go-bag, and his rule: never be somewhere you can't leave. Emotional beat: controlled unease beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Flight 409
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He escorts the delegation aboard a chartered flight to Geneva for the summit. Mid-air, a junior analyst quietly notes the flight's transponder record has already been scrubbed from tracking databases. Lior dismisses it as a glitch. Beat: first hairline crack in his certainty.

chapters.title: One Passenger Fewer
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The plane lands; manifest reconciliation fails — eleven boarded, ten disembarked. The missing man is Tomas Reiner, a quiet 'consultant' Lior never liked. Authorities move suspiciously fast to call it a clerical error. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Odile
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Introduced in Geneva, tailing the summit security chief. She's hunting Reiner too — her contract predates his disappearance, and a dead target pays nothing. She notices Lior watching the same doors. Beat: cold competence laced with private irritation.

chapters.title: The Scrubbed Man
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Digging into Reiner's identity, Lior finds every record dissolving in real time — passports, employment, even hotel CCTV overwritten. Someone with state-level reach is erasing a living man. Beat: vertigo; the erasure mirrors what was once done to Lior himself.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She maps which agencies are stonewalling: French intelligence denies the charter existed, Swiss police lost the arrival footage, and a US liaison offers her money to stop asking. She realizes the summit's security framework is the buried secret. Beat: predatory focus sharpening.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lior and Odile confront each other in a lakeside parking garage — knife drawn, then lowered when each realizes the other holds half the truth. Uneasy truce: forty-eight hours until the summit convenes. Beat: wary mutual recognition.

chapters.title: What Reiner Carried
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A dead-drop cache reveals Reiner's evidence: documents proving the summit's surveillance architecture was built using black-site data — and naming the contractors who laundered it, including a young operative called 'M. Marchetti.' Beat: the floor giving way beneath him.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Itinerary
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Reconstructing Reiner's last week through pawn tickets and burner calls, she concludes he never left the airport — he's hidden inside its maintenance warren, hiding from both governments and assassins. Beat: grim admiration for the prey.

chapters.title: Terminal 2
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They find Reiner alive but broken, refusing to surface because surfacing means death by paperwork. He gives them a key: a ledger stored on a server only accessible during the summit itself. Beat: desperate hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: The Handler
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. His old handler resurfaces, offering reinstatement and protection if Lior hands over Reiner and forgets the ledger. The offer is generous, which is how Lior knows it's a trap. Beat: temptation and disgust in equal measure.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Hiding Reiner in a safehouse, she calculates exits and betrayal odds, and finds herself uncharacteristically unwilling to cut losses on two liabilities. A quiet scene where Reiner asks why she kills, and she doesn't answer. Beat: humanity leaking through armor.

chapters.title: Breach
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The safehouse is hit by a team too professional to be police. Reiner is taken; Odile and Lior escape separately, each now certain there's a leak between them. Beat: fury and suspicion braided together.

chapters.title: The Mole in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Tracing the breach team's comms, she discovers the orders originated from Lior's own old unit — meaning someone sold his history to buy his silence. She chooses, deliberately, not to tell him yet. Beat: loyalty tested against strategy.

chapters.title: Confession at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Cornered in a train yard, Lior confesses everything — his real crimes, his bought identity — to Odile, expecting her contract to expand to include him. Instead she tears up the paper. Beat: raw exposure; the lie finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Geneva locks down. Delegations arrive; the security architecture goes live; Reiner sits in a black site above the lake, scheduled to become a permanent ghost after the closing ceremony. Beat: ticking clock made audible.

chapters.title: The Ledger Key
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She infiltrates the summit venue as catering staff, mapping server access points, while Lior leverages his contractor credentials to get inside the perimeter one last time. Beat: cold, precise suspense.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A violent, tightly choreographed extraction of Reiner from the black site — alarms, a stairwell fight, Odile wounded shielding him. They get him out, barely, as the summit's opening session begins below. Beat: adrenaline cresting.

chapters.title: The Floor of the Summit
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Rather than flee, Lior walks Reiner into the press gallery of the opening session and forces the ledger onto the venue's own screens. Three delegations freeze; the security chief lunges; cameras catch everything. Beat: triumphant self-immolation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the chaos, she could kill anyone she wants. Instead she covers Lior's exit, settles her original contract as 'target unrecoverable,' and disappears into the crowd. Beat: release; the assassin choosing to put the weapon down, for today.

chapters.title: Inquiries
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Hearings, leaks, resignations — the summit collapses into scandal, and Lior testifies under his real name for the first time in fifteen years. He loses every client and sleeps properly for the first time in longer. Beat: costly, earned peace.

chapters.title: Odile and the Ghost
chapters.summary: Dual POV epilogue. Months later, on a Portuguese coast, Lior runs a two-man consultancy with nothing to hide. A postcard arrives with no signature — just a drawing of a bird. Somewhere, Reiner lives openly under a new name that is finally his own. Beat: quiet, watchful hope.
